zh.CATEGORY: B2B 协作 / AI 工作平台（工作操作系统 + Agent 托管层）
zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它卖的不是聊天，是「把任意业务动作变成频道里一次可被 @ 的调用」；2026 年它的赌注不是造更强的模型，是当 agent 的家——双向 MCP + Skills + 权限模型，让别人家的 AI 住进来。
zh.USER_SCALE: 可核实的都是营销口径：10 亿+ 每日已发送消息、400 万 Slack Connect 用户每周与外部团队协作、300 万每日工作流、170 万每周活跃使用的应用（官网脚注分别标 2026 财年财报发言 / 2025 财年内部数据 / Salesforce 内部数据）。Marketplace 官方口径 2,600+ 应用，sitemap 实测 2,871 个应用页（另有 9 个合集页 + 1 个首页 = 2,881 条）。G2 4.5 分 / 40,606 条评论，分布 5★75% · 4★20% · 3★3% · 2★0% · 1★0%。DAU/MAU、付费席位数、ARR：官方未单独披露，本卡不编。Product Hunt 页本次被 Cloudflare 拦截，无数据可用。
zh.STAGE_MATURITY: 成熟期，且正在换第二曲线。四个付费档（Free / Pro / Business+ / Enterprise+）明码标价；13 个语种站点；199 个客户故事；Marketplace（2,881 页）、帮助中心（579 页）、开发者文档（3,266 页）三套独立信息架构各跑各的。AI 侧从「Slack AI 摘要」长到「Slackbot + 双向 MCP + Agentforce + code channels」。历史节点：2013-08 发布（24 小时 8,000 个客户）→ 2019-06 直接上市（195 亿美元）→ 2021-07-21 归入 Salesforce（约 277 亿美元）→ 2023-03 接 ChatGPT → 2025-05 Agentforce 进 Slack → 2025-06 开始阻止 LLM 长期索引/复制数据。
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Freemium + 按席位订阅 + 企业年付。Free $0 永久（90 天消息历史、最多 10 个 app、1:1 huddle/DM）；Pro $8.75 每人每月（年付 $7.25）；Business+ $18（年付 $15，Slackbot 持续可用）；Enterprise+ $45（仅年付，Slackbot 无周消息上限）。AI 超额用量走 Salesforce Flex Credits；非营利/教育有折扣；Frontline 是附加组件（均见定价页 FAQ）。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: 它是把业务动作标准化成消息流原子的协议层；AI 时代它不争「谁的模型强」，争「agent 住在谁家」。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 拔电测试判为嵌入型：拿走 Slackbot 与 AI 摘要，频道、Slack Connect、Canvas、List、Huddle、Workflow Builder 都照常卖——AI 不是地基，是长在地基上的第二层。它的护城河也不在功能表上，在接入协议 + 权限模型 + 工作场所占据：2,600+ 应用愿意接它，是因为它先定义了身份、权限、事件与消息格式，生态替它长功能。代价是它的每一次 AI 升级都必须以「已有形态」出现——agent 得是一个能被 @ 的成员，而不是一个新 App。
zh.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: 护城河是协议，不是功能
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: 12 个原子（Channel / Canvas / List / Message / Huddle / App / Agent / Slackbot / Workflow / MCP tool / Search / 权限）拼出四种封装：Template 给人、Slackbot Skills 给团队方法、Agent + 双向 MCP 给机器、Workflow Builder 给流程。它不自己长全部功能，让 2,600+ 应用替它长——所以功能表永远追不上，接入位永远在。
zh.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: AI 的计价单位从席位换成额度
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 定价页原文：Free 与 Pro 的 Slackbot 只是 limited trial，Business+ 与 Enterprise+ 才持续可用，只有 Enterprise+ 写 no weekly message limits，超额买 Salesforce Flex Credits；Workflow Builder 则是 Pro 起的付费功能。两条放在一起说明：AI 在它这里不是加量项，是分档线——这也是 2026 年 SaaS 定价最值得盯的一处变化。
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 流量是一座 13 语种的大站，不是一条爆款
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: sitemap 实测（2026-11-26）：营销站英文 1,769 页，13 个语种各一份（zh-CN 1,478 页），其中 blog 1,179 页是最大单一板块；Marketplace 2,881 页；帮助中心 579 页（578 篇 × 13 语言）。对比页两套并存：产品级 /compare/slack-vs-teams、/compare/slack-vs-email，博客级 /blog/compare/* 18 条（13 个竞品 vs 页 + 4 个 alternatives 页 + 1 个德语法务页）。这是典型的「大站 + 目录 + 帮助中心」三件套，不靠单篇爆款。
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: 产品定位：Slack 是团队与企业的协作工作场所——把对话、文档、任务、会议、跨组织协作与 AI 放进同一个壳里。官方 2026 年的措辞是 The platform agents and AI call home：它把自己定义成 agent 的运行底座，而不只是一个聊天工具。一句更直白的判断：它为「一家 20 到 20,000 人的公司」解决「这件事该在哪儿说、谁来接、以后去哪儿找」这三件反复发生的事。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官方 H1 原文：All your people and AI agents working together；副标 Slack connects your team. Slackbot multiplies what they can do。翻成用户语言：你不用再决定「这件事该发消息、发邮件还是建个任务」，都在一个地方；AI 也不是另一个网站，而是同一个地方里能被 @ 的队友。
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 团队与企业（10 人到 10 万人）
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: 这是它真正收钱的一层。买的是「频道即容器」：一个话题一个频道，人、文件、应用、AI 都在里面，权限边界就是频道边界。往上走，付费理由从「历史无限」逐步换成「治理」——多工作区、细分角色、信息屏障、法定保留、Discovery API、HIPAA。官方 Solutions 把场景切成 9 个部门 × 9 个行业 × 11 个 use case（共 32 个 solutions 页），说明它卖的不是单点工具，而是每个职能的工作场所。
zh.SEGMENT_2_NAME: 开发者 / IT（做集成与治理的人）
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: 这一层不进定价页，进文档站：359 个 Web API 方法页、121 个事件页、129 个 scope 页、46 个 block element、22 个 block、3,266 个文档 URL；Slack CLI 90 个命令页，Bolt 三语言 SDK，Deno SDK，8 个官方 samples。他们是它真正的渠道：2,600+ 应用和每一个内部 agent 都从这一层长出来，而 IT 又是 Business+/Enterprise+ 的付款批准人。
zh.SEGMENT_3_NAME: 跨组织协作者（客户、供应商、代理商）
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Slack Connect 把外部组织拉进同一批频道与 DM（Pro 以上最多 250 个 orgs），官方措辞是 moving conversations out of siloed email threads。这一层的战略价值不在收费，在分发：每一次跨公司协作都是一次产品露出，且对方公司往往还没有 Slack——这是它少见的「病毒环长在 B 端」的结构。
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 让一件事在同一个地方被说清、被决定、被跟踪，而不是在邮件、IM、文档、工单之间搬。
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 不怕漏掉关键消息，也不被消息淹掉。G2 的 5 星用户写下的不满几乎全是同一件事：通知太多、重要的东西被埋在频道里、旧上下文不好找。它卖的安全感是「我能找到」，而用户真实的体验常常是「我得从一堆里翻出来」。
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 在组织里成为「知道去哪儿问、知道谁在负责」的那个人；对外部伙伴，则是「你被拉进了我们的频道」这种被接纳感。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 团队从 8 人涨到 20 人，微信/邮件/线下开始丢上下文：同一个问题被问三遍，新人入职要靠人带。Slack 的入口不是「我要一个聊天工具」，是「我们要一个能沉淀的地方」。
zh.FREQUENCY: 按工作日持续在线，一天数十次到上百次；官方口径每日已发送消息 10 亿+（2026 财年财报发言），单用户频次未披露。
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 桌面 / 移动 / 网页三端；会议在频道内用 Huddle；行动项落到 Canvas 或 List；跨公司走 Connect；检索走 Enterprise Search 与 AI 搜索；执行走 Workflow Builder、Slackbot 与被 @ 的 agent；数据出口是 MCP server、Web API 与 Events。
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 触发点不是「我要用 AI」，是「这件事得有人接」。Slack 的高明之处在于：它没有为 AI 造新入口，所有 AI 都长在已有容器上——输入框、频道、画布、列表。用户不需要学一个新动作，只需要把 @ 换成 @Slackbot。
zh.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: 在输入框里 @ 一下，或者让它自己跑
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 同一个输入框承担三种动作：@ 一个 agent / 跑一条 workflow / 把消息转成 List 的一行。Workflow Builder 支持触发器 + 步骤 + 条件（官方写 up to 15 conditions）+ 70+ 连接器；Slackbot 可以调你的 MCP server，官方给了 4 种鉴权方式（无鉴权 / Slack 身份 / DCR / 手动 OAuth）。动作入口的收敛，是它把「AI 变成习惯」而非「AI 变成功能」的关键。
zh.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: 答案、记录、下一步都留在对话流里
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: 结果不需要切到另一个界面看：Slackbot 的产物可以是频道里一张可排序、可筛选、可固定的视图，Huddle 结束后自动出笔记与 action items，Canvas 里能直接放工作流。把产出留在「事情发生的地方」，是它和所有「打开一个新 App 干活」的 AI 产品最大的差别。
zh.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: 频道变厚，历史变成资产
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 回来的理由不是「再聊一次」，是「上次那事在哪个频道决定的」。频道 + 线程 + Canvas + List 构成一份不可搬迁的组织记忆，Enterprise Search 再把它和已连接的第三方应用缝在一起。免费档只给 90 天历史，恰恰说明「历史」在这门生意里值钱。
zh.LOOP_FREQ: 每天数十次到上百次（[推断] 依据：官方 10 亿+ 每日消息 ÷ 企业工作日；单用户打开频次与 DAU 未披露）。
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 同一个触发反复出现：一件事发生了，得有人在频道里接住它。它把这个动作从「找人私聊」改成「在频道里公开说一次」，于是信息从一对多变成多对多——这是它真正的产品主张，也是它制造通知过载的原因。
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 它真正教用户的是「工作不需要被归档到别处」：对话本身就是记录，@ 一下就是执行。用久之后，人会开始按「有没有频道」判断一件事值不值得做。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 流量曝光：三条腿并行，权重从大到小（[推断]，依据是页面结构与 CTA 设计）。① 产品内 PLG + 团队自传播：所有页面 CTA 是 Get started、无销售介入，模板与 Skills 可一键落进工作区并组织级发布；② 大站 SEO：英文营销站 1,769 页 + Marketplace 2,881 页 + 帮助中心 579 页，13 个语种各一份，blog 1,179 篇是最大单一板块；③ Salesforce 企业渠道：官网署名旗下公司、Slackbot 进 Lightning、Flex Credits 走 Salesforce 售卖，每页并行 Talk to sales。自然搜索流量占比、各渠道 CAC、Marketplace 带来的注册占比：均未核验，不推测。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 官方叙事里最像 aha 的一刻是：在频道里 @Slackbot 让它调你自己的 MCP server，工具结果直接回到 thread 里——不是打开一个新 App，是「队友多了一个」。本期未实测，这一点只据官方功能页与文档描述，不作体验结论。
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 有，而且是结构性的，只是不长得像病毒传播：Slack Connect 把外部组织拉进同一批频道（Pro 以上 250 orgs），跨公司协作本身就是曝光；模板与 Slackbot Skills 的组织级发布，让「一个人的方法」变成「全队一键可跑」，这是内部扩散。分享数据官方未披露，本条为 [推断]。
zh.RETENTION_1: 频道历史 + 线程 + Canvas + List 构成组织记忆，迁移等于把记忆留在原地（免费档只给 90 天，付费买的就是这段记忆）。
zh.RETENTION_2: 2,600+ 应用的集成位与 OAuth 授权关系一旦铺开，换工具等于重做一遍接入与审批。
zh.RETENTION_3: 治理层：信息屏障、法定保留、Discovery API、DLP、app approvals——这一层是 IT 愿意续费的原因，也是最难搬的部分。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_NAME: 免费档 → 团队 → 治理的爬梯环
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Free $0 永久（90 天历史、10 个 app）→ 团队涨到需要无限历史与无限 app（Pro $8.75）→ 需要 Slackbot 持续可用与合规（Business+ $18）→ 需要多 SAML、data residency、Slackbot 无周上限（Enterprise+ $45）。四级台阶每一级都绑一个「组织才需要」的能力，这是它把个人使用转成企业付费的标准路径。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: 第三方应用上架 Marketplace 拿分发 → 每个应用一页贡献长尾（sitemap 2,871 个应用页）→ 用户为了某个 app 装 Slack → 该 app 的作者又成了 Slack 的分销。它自己不用多写一页内容，目录会替它长。这条环的脆弱点在于：平台一旦收紧审核或 API 权限（它 2025-06 已开始阻止 LLM 长期索引），环的转速会立刻下降。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 产品的容器，也是权限的边界：一个话题一个频道，人、文件、应用、AI 全在里面。官方措辞是 flexible, transparent spaces for working together。Slack 所有 AI 能力都长在这个容器上，而不是另起一个界面。
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 把外部组织拉进同一批频道与 DM（Pro 以上最多 250 orgs），官方定位是把对话从割裂的邮件线程里搬出来。它是 B 端少见的病毒入口：合作方被迫成为用户。
zh.SURFACE_3_NAME: Canvas + List（文档与结构化数据）
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Canvas 是频道里的文档面，也是 Slackbot Skills 的指令载体（官方写 with a canvas you own）；List 是会话内的任务表，可被工作流读写、可被 MCP server 增删改查。这两件是它从「聊天」跨到「工作」的桥。
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: 频道内即时音视频与异步录制；Huddle 结束后 AI 自动出笔记、待办与谁说了什么。会议不再是另一个软件，而是频道里的一次举手。
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: Slackbot 是团队级 AI 队友（跨应用执行：调研、建工作流、建 dashboard/报表、更新记录、起草内容），Agent 是可被 @ 的成员级实体，两者靠 Skills（markdown/canvas 指令 → 组织级发布）与双向 MCP 长出能力。这一层是它在 2026 年真正的产品重心。
zh.SURFACE_6_NAME: Workflow Builder + Enterprise Search（编排与检索）
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 编排层：触发器 + 步骤 + 条件（最多 15 个条件）+ 70+ 连接器，可插 AI 生成回答、agent 对话、自定义代码步骤，Pro 起付费。检索层：一个搜索框搜 Slack + 已连接应用 + 自建数据源（Custom Sources API），权限感知。前者把重复流程变成自动跑，后者把组织记忆变成可查——它们才是「工作 OS」这个词的实处。
zh.ENTITY_1: Workspace / Org（工作区，计费与权限的最小单位）
zh.ENTITY_3: Message / Thread（对话的最小单元与从属线程）
zh.ENTITY_4: Canvas / List / Workflow（文档、结构化记录、自动化）
zh.ENTITY_5: App / Agent / Skill / MCP server（身份与工具，可被 @ 的执行者）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 主轴是「频道」：一切从频道进来，再横向串成搜索、Connect 与治理。好处是零学习成本——频道本来就是团队的心智单位；代价是产品没有自己的画布，所有价值都寄存在「对话是否发生在这里」这件事上。也正因为这样，它才必须把 AI 做成频道里的一个成员：新界面会破坏这个主轴，新成员不会。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 结构是「左侧频道栏 + 顶部搜索 + 底部输入框」三段式，输入框同时是消息、workflow、agent 调用与文件上传的入口——把所有动作收进一个框，是它交互上最省事也最有效的设计。本期未实测，此段只据官方功能页与文档结构描述，不写体验结论。
zh.CRAFT_1_NAME: 把 AI 做成「成员」，不做成「按钮」
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: Slackbot 的身份是一个能被 @ 的队友，而不是工具栏里的一个按钮。这个选择决定了三件事：AI 有权限、有上下文、有历史；人不需要切换界面；以及它在频道里的产出天然被别人看见（也就天然可被复用）。
zh.CRAFT_2_NAME: 三种封装分层，各卖给不同的人
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Template 卖给「不想从零配」的团队（预配置 channel + canvas + list + workflow）；Slackbot Skills 卖给「有自己方法」的人（一段 markdown 或一个 canvas → 组织级发布 → 全队一键跑）；Agent + 双向 MCP 卖给「有工程能力」的组织。同一批原子，三种包装，三种买家。
zh.CRAFT_3_NAME: 把「个人绝活」变成「组织资产」的机制
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: Skills 的四步是：用 markdown 或 canvas 写指令 → 创建 → 更新 → 组织级发布（API 名 admin.slackbot.skills.publish）→ 加入成员库。这是知识库产品化的标准形态：规则写成文件、发布成能力、按需调用。它把「老员工的经验」从口头变成了可执行资产。
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 双向 MCP：既当服务器，也当客户端
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: 一头是 Slack MCP Server（https://mcp.slack.com/mcp，远程 HTTP + OAuth），让 Claude、Cursor 这类外部 AI 读写 Slack 的消息、频道、Canvas、List；另一头是 Slackbot MCP Client，让 Slack 连你自己的远程 MCP server，自动发现并调用其中工具。「你家的 AI 可以进我家；我家的 AI 也可以去你家」——这是 2026 年平台级产品最难抄的一步。
zh.CRAFT_5_NAME: 把 AI 用量做成定价的档位线
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Free/Pro 的 Slackbot 是 limited trial，Business+/Enterprise+ 才持续可用，只有 Enterprise+ 写 no weekly message limits，超额走 Salesforce Flex Credits。它没有公布具体条数——模糊的额度本身就是一种定价权。对用户的启示：按「AI 执行量」而不是只按人头计价，会是 2026 年 SaaS 的默认动作。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 所有工艺都指向一句话：让新能力以「已有形态」出现。agent 是成员、技能是文件、自动化是频道里的一个步骤——用户不需要学新东西，只需要把旧动作多做一次。
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：本次未测（本期没有实测；不把「第一次收到消息」当成价值到达，也不换算成分钟）
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 可核实的只有结构：注册 → 建工作区 → 邀请成员 → 建频道 → 装应用/配 workflow。真正的 aha 通常不是产品给的，是同事给的（有人在你建的频道里回了话）。官方未披露 onboarding 数据，本报告不给时间数字。
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：中（未实测；可核实的结构是同一个界面里并存四种容器：频道、线程、画布、列表）
zh.DELIGHT_1: 模板可以一键落进工作区：channel + canvas + list + workflow 整套骨架，不用从空白页开始（官方 35 个模板 + 14 个分类）。
zh.DELIGHT_2: Huddle 开完自动出笔记与 action items，会议不需要换软件（官方功能页原文）。
zh.DELIGHT_3: @ 一个 agent 就开一个 code channel，人 + 队友 + agent 在频道里共同看 diff（code channels 功能页）。
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜点：模板一键生成工作场所、会议自动留痕、agent 变成频道成员
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任：大众口碑很稳（G2 4.5 / 40,606，1★与 2★各占 0%），企业信任层按档位给（信息屏障、法定保留、Discovery API、HIPAA 在 Business+ 起，多 SAML 与 data residency 在 Enterprise+）。但信任的真实瓶颈不在安全，在噪音：5 星用户的最大不满就是「重要的东西被埋了」。
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 通知过载与信息被埋：G2 差评原话 The notification overload can get pretty overwhelming once you're in a few active channel, important updates get buried fast；5 星用户也重复同一句。这是「一切进频道」的直接代价。
zh.STRUGGLE_2: 免费档的墙很硬：90 天消息历史、最多 10 个 app、1:1 huddle。G2 原话点名 the 90-day message history limit on the free tier is really annoying。
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 学习曲线与界面复杂度：G2 差评原话 The interface was too hard to use. Not user-friendly enough；另一条写 it makes it incredibly hard to follow and use unless you are on it 24x7。
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 摩擦：通知过载、免费档的墙、学习曲线
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Freemium + 按席位订阅 + 企业年付（AI 额度做分档线）
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Free $0（90 天历史 / 10 个 app / 1:1 huddle 与外部 DM / Basic AI）；Pro $8.75 每人每月，年付 $7.25（无限历史、无限 app、群组 huddle、最多 250 个外部组织）；Business+ $18，年付 $15（Slackbot 持续可用 + 管理合规套件）；Enterprise+ $45，仅年付、Contact Sales（Slackbot 无周消息上限 + Enterprise search + 多 SAML + data residency）。促销价（Pro $4.38、Business+ $9，前三个月）与 Flex Credits 超额购买都在定价页 FAQ 里写明。
zh.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: 入口免费到能自传播，钱收在治理与 AI 额度上
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: 免费档给的是「一个团队能真的用起来」的最小集合（90 天历史 + 10 个 app + 1:1 会议），刚好卡在「小团队够用、成长中的团队一定不够」的位置。付费的三次跳：无限历史与无限 app（Pro）→ Slackbot 持续可用 + 合规（Business+）→ 多 SAML / data residency / 无周上限（Enterprise+）。它卖的不是功能，是「组织变大之后必须有的那几样东西」。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: 免费：90 天消息历史、最多 10 个 app、1:1 huddle、1:1 外部 DM、Basic AI（摘要 / Slackbot 试用 / AI 工作流生成 / AI 搜索 / 每日回顾 / 文件摘要）。付费：Pro 买无限历史、无限 app、群组 huddle、最多 250 个外部组织；Business+ 买 Slackbot 持续可用与治理（多工作区、细分角色、信息屏障、法定保留、Discovery API、HIPAA）；Enterprise+ 买 Slackbot 无周消息上限、Enterprise search、多 SAML、data residency。另外 Workflow Builder 是 Pro 起的付费功能，AI 超额走 Flex Credits。
zh.UX_MON_HEADLINE: 体验与变现是对齐的，还是打架的？
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 大体对齐，但 2026 年出现了一道新裂缝。对齐的一面：免费档卡在「团队会自然撞墙」的位置（历史、app 数、群组会议），付费墙全部落在组织变大后才需要的东西上（治理、合规、AI 额度），切得很准。打架的一面：AI 的计价从「席位」变成「Slackbot 额度」，而额度数值官方不公布——用户没法预算「我这个月会花多少 AI」，这会让采购在续约时把不确定性折成折扣。另一处张力：Workflow Builder 到底算不算免费档能力，功能页说是付费功能、定价页 Free 档又列了 AI workflow generation，官方口径自相矛盾。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 同一批企业员工：已经在用 Microsoft 365 的公司
zh.COMP_1_D2: 长在 Microsoft 365 栈里（Outlook / SharePoint / Office 同账号），会议走 Teams；本次未核验其对外协议细节
zh.COMP_1_D3: 企业批量授权与 IT 采购，默认随 M365 到位
zh.COMP_1_D4: 本次未核验（Slack 官网把它列进 /compare/slack-vs-teams 与博客 13 个竞品 vs 页之首）
zh.COMP_2_D1: Workspace 客户：Gmail / Drive / Meet 已经在用的团队
zh.COMP_2_D2: 与 Gmail、Drive、Meet 同栈，账号体系即权限体系
zh.COMP_2_D3: Workspace 默认位，零分发成本
zh.COMP_2_D4: 本次未核验（Slack 博客有 /blog/compare/slack-vs-google-chat）
zh.COMP_3_D1: 社群与兴趣团体起家，正往工作场景渗透的小团队
zh.COMP_3_D2: 频道 + 语音房，为「在场感」设计，不以权限与治理为第一优先
zh.COMP_3_D3: 社区自传播与创作者生态，几乎不靠企业销售
zh.COMP_3_D4: 本次未核验（Slack 博客有 /blog/compare/slack-vs-discord）
zh.COMP_4_NAME: 自托管与合规替代（Mattermost / Chatwork / Line Works / Stackfield）
zh.COMP_4_D1: 数据不能出内网、或所在市场被本地产品占住的组织
zh.COMP_4_D2: 自托管或本地化部署，用「数据不出门」换掉一部分功能
zh.COMP_4_D3: 政企采购、地区渠道、开源社区
zh.COMP_4_D4: 本次未核验（这四家都在 Slack 博客的竞品 vs 页名单里，说明它自己把它们当对手）
zh.COMP_OWN_D1: 团队协作工作场所 + agent 托管层
zh.COMP_OWN_D2: 双向 MCP（server + client）+ 2,600+ 应用 + 可 @ 的 agent + Real-Time Search API
zh.COMP_OWN_D3: 13 语种大站（英文 1,769 页）+ Marketplace 2,881 页 + 帮助中心 579 页 + Salesforce 渠道
zh.COMP_OWN_D4: 四档明码标价，Slackbot 额度做分档线，超额 Flex Credits；但具体额度数值不公开
zh.COMP_INTRO: 名单不靠猜，取自它自己的动作：官网产品级对比页只有两个（/compare/slack-vs-teams、/compare/slack-vs-email），但博客级 /blog/compare/* 有 18 条，其中 13 条是竞品 vs 页——asana、chatwork、clickup、discord、google-chat、line-works、mattermost、microsoft-teams、monday、stackfield、trello、whatsapp、zoom，另有 4 条 alternatives 页（teams / discord / google-chat / trello 的替代品）。换句话说：它把 Microsoft Teams 当正面战场，把 Google Chat 与 Discord 当侧翼，把 mattermost / chatwork / line-works / stackfield 当「本地化与自托管」这一路的防守对象。竞品价格本次全部未核验，不编。
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 三处别人短期不好补：一是双向 MCP（别家多是单向接入，Slack 同时做了 server 与 client）；二是应用目录的厚度（2,600+ 应用，sitemap 2,871 页，且每个应用自带一页长尾）；三是治理颗粒度（信息屏障、法定保留、Discovery API、app approvals 这一整套，是它从 Pro 走到 Enterprise+ 的真正台阶）。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 三条缝：平台捆绑（Teams 随 M365、Google Chat 随 Workspace 到位，用户不会为同一件事再买一份）；通知过载（G2 的 5 星用户都在抱怨，这是它自己长出来的结构性问题，而 Discord 这类产品把噪音当成氛围）；AI 额度不透明（Slackbot 限额不公布，采购算不出账，恰恰给了竞品一个「打包价更好算」的切口）。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 高意图与本地化 SEO 双轨：13 个语种各一份营销站（英文 1,769 页、zh-CN 1,478 页），blog 1,179 篇是最大单一板块；产品级对比页 2 个 + 博客级竞品 vs 页 13 个 + alternatives 页 4 个；定价还被拆成 /pricing/free、/pricing/pro、/pricing/businessplus、/pricing/paid-vs-free 四个独立入口承接搜索。
zh.CHANNEL_2: PLG 免费档与团队自传播：所有页面 CTA 是 Get started、无销售介入；模板可一键落进工作区；Skills 可组织级发布——「一个人的方法变成全队一键可跑」本身就是内部扩散机制。
zh.CHANNEL_3: Salesforce 企业渠道 + Partner 体系：官网署名 Salesforce 旗下公司，Slackbot 进 Lightning，Flex Credits 走 Salesforce 售卖；另有 Partner Program、Partner Offers、Slack Certified 与 199 个客户故事支撑采购决策。
zh.FRICTION_1_TITLE: 通知过载：一切进频道的代价
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: G2 里 5 星用户写下的不满高度一致：重要更新被淹没、旧上下文难找、通知分心。这不是 bug，是「一切进频道」这个设计选择的另一面——同一个机制既带来透明，也带来噪音。对它的 AI 来说这是一道真正的题：摘要与每日回顾只是在噪音上加一层摘要，真正的解法是「什么该打扰我」的判断权。
zh.FRICTION_2_TITLE: 免费档的墙刚好卡在团队长大那一刻
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: 90 天历史 + 10 个 app + 1:1 huddle：单看每一项都不算苛刻，合起来就是「小团队试用很爽、真用会撞墙」。G2 原话点名 90 天历史 annoying。这是设计意图，不是缺陷——但也意味着它对「三个人的小团队」几乎没有收入，收入必须靠团队长大，这把增长曲线的斜率交给了客户的招聘节奏。
zh.FRICTION_3_TITLE: 学习曲线与界面复杂度
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: G2 差评原话：The interface was too hard to use. Not user-friendly enough；另一条写，除非你 24x7 挂在上面，否则很难跟上它在说什么。对内部沟通工具，这等于说「信息架构的复杂度已经超过了组织的信息量」。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: AI 计价不透明：限额不公布
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 定价页只说 Free/Pro 的 Slackbot 是 limited trial、Enterprise+ 没有周消息上限，具体条数不公布；超额要买 Salesforce Flex Credits。对采购，这意味着 AI 这一项不可预算；对竞品，这是最好的切入话术。同一份定价里还有一处矛盾未解：Workflow Builder 功能页说是付费功能，定价页 Free 档却列了 AI workflow generation。
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方未单独披露运营指标。以下分两类：能核实的公开事实（价格、sitemap 页数、G2 评级分布、官方营销数字），与标注 [推断] 的「它应该看什么」——后者不是真实数据。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 每周在频道内被完成的「动作」数（被 @ 的 agent 调用 + 跑完的 workflow + 被关闭的 List 项）（[推断]）
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [推断] 它按席位收费、按「工作是否在这里发生」定价：消息量只证明热闹，动作数才证明它是工作场所。北美星不该是 DAU——Slack 的 DAU 早已饱和，2026 年真正要证明的是「AI 有没有被真的用起来」。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: 免费档 → 付费档的历史解锁率（90 天前的消息被读了几次）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 免费档唯一会「疼」的墙是 90 天历史。查过 90 天前消息的团队，才是有真实记忆需求的团队；这个行为比注册数更能预测付费。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: Slackbot 的周活跃与 Skills 的组织级发布数
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Slackbot 是它 AI 收入的唯一分档线；Skills 的组织级发布数则说明「个人方法有没有变成组织资产」——后者是它相对所有 AI 助手最独特的留存机制。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: Marketplace 应用的安装深度（安装后 30 天仍在用）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: 2,881 页应用目录是它的长尾与护城河，但目录的价值取决于「装上的应用有没有被用」，不是应用数量。装而不用会让生态从资产变成噪音。
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: 每用户每日通知数 + 关键消息被读到的延迟
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: G2 的 5 星用户都在抱怨同一件事：重要的东西被埋。通知量是增长最诚实的反向指标——通知越多活跃可能越高，但价值越低。这条护栏不设，AI 摘要只会让噪音更贵。
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: 没有公开的付费席位流失率、ARR 拆分、单条消息的推理成本 [推断]
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [推断] Slackbot「按席位固定成本、不按 token 计费」的口径意味着它在替用户吞掉推理成本的不确定性；免费档也在用 AI，等于免费用户持续烧钱。如果只看活跃与评论，会看不见「AI 用得越多、毛利越薄」。另一处盲区：它 2025-06 开始阻止 LLM 长期索引，短期看是护数据，长期会影响它在 AI 答案里的可见度——这条不会出现在任何产品指标里。
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 协议与权限 9、分发与目录 9、工作场所占据 9、AI 能力 6、独立定价权 5（Salesforce 旗下）、防 AI 抓取 7，加权 8：能被复制的是功能，难复制的是「2,600 个应用已经按你的身份与权限模型写好了」。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 从沟通到执行：Workflow Builder、Slackbot 现场产物、Slack CRM——把对话末端接上流程与业务对象。
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: 从人到 agent：Agent、code channels、双向 MCP——把「同事」这个概念扩展到非人类成员（[推断] 这是它唯一能躲开「又一个聊天工具」的方向）。
zh.VERTICAL_1: 9 个部门 × 9 个行业：Frontline、Engineering、IT、客服、销售、项目管理、市场、HR、安全，加制造/金融/零售/公共部门/教育/医疗。
zh.VERTICAL_2: 11 个 use case 页（项目管理、客户协作、高效会议、销售管道、内部沟通、项目跟踪、线索管理、团队生产力、入职、工时、快速找答案）——它把「所有需要协作的岗位」都铺了一遍。
zh.PLATFORM_1: 开放接口已经齐了：Slack MCP Server（远程 HTTP + OAuth）、Slackbot MCP Client（4 种鉴权）、Web API（359 个方法页）、Events（121 个）、Real-Time Search API、Block Kit、Bolt 三语言 SDK、Deno SDK、CLI、8 个官方 samples。
zh.PLATFORM_2: [推断] 它的平台策略是「当 agent 的托管层」：不争谁来当助手，争助手住在哪里。被 Salesforce 收编之后，这个策略反而更顺——因为 Salesforce 需要一个企业侧的 agent 落地场所，而 Slack 正好是那个场所。
zh.OPP_1_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把「Skills → 组织资产」这套机制抄成知识库产品
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: 怎么做：用 markdown 或画布写指令 → 组织级发布 → 全队一键跑，四步照抄 Slackbot Skills 的结构（创建/更新/发布/入成员库），但落地在一个更窄的场景里（比如某个岗位的固定流程）。为什么：这是把「老员工的判断」变成可执行资产的最短路径，而绝大多数知识库产品还停在「文档存起来」，没走到「能力被调用」。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: （我的判断）先做协议/插件，不做又一个界面
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: 怎么做：把产品做成 MCP server + 一个 Skill 包，去别人的场景里被调用（Claude、Cursor、Slackbot 都能是宿主），而不是要求用户再装一个 App。为什么：Slack 证明了「定义好身份+权限+事件+消息格式，生态会替你长功能」；对资源少的团队，这是唯一能借到别人分发的方式。
zh.OPP_3_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把定价单位从人头改成执行量，但要把额度写明
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: 怎么做：设一档按「AI 执行量」计价（而不是只按人头），并且把额度数值、超额单价、用量面板全部写清。为什么：Slack 已经把分档线从席位挪到 Slackbot 额度，但额度不公布——这既是它的定价权，也是它的采购阻力。照抄方向、反着做透明度，是最省力的差异化。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 它的赌注：不造最强的 AI，做 AI 必须住的房子
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: 三个动作叠在一起：把 AI 做成频道成员（Slackbot / Agent / Skills）而不是新界面；用双向 MCP 让外部 agent 能进能出；用权限与治理把「企业敢让 agent 上手」这件事做实。前两个是产品动作，第三个才是真赌注——因为 agent 真正卡住的从来不是能力，是「它能不能被授权去动真实数据」。代价是它必须持续妥协：为了让 2,600 个应用继续适配，它的每一项 AI 能力都得兼容旧形态，创新速度被生态绑架。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 终局：工作不再有「入口」，只有「谁被叫到」
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: 如果 agent 真的成为同事，那么「打开一个工作软件」这个动作会消失——人只需要说话，agent 自己去调工具、留记录、找下一个执行者。在那种世界里，赢家不是模型最强的，而是「身份、权限、上下文、审计」四件事都在它手里的那一家。Slack 现在的位置离这个终局最近，但它缺两块：一是自己的模型（它选择不造，靠合作），二是跨出 Slack 的上下文（2025-06 阻止 LLM 索引，恰恰说明它不愿意把上下文交出去）。这两块决定了它是「agent 的家」还是「agent 的宿舍」。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 风险按「可能性 × 影响」排序，严重度是我的判断，不是公司披露。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 平台捆绑：Teams 与 Google Chat 把「聊天」做成免费默认
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 守住捆绑做不到的三件：跨公司协作（Connect 的网络）、应用目录的厚度、双向 MCP 的开放性。同时把「治理」当成正面卖点打——捆绑品最难做的就是信息屏障与法定保留这一层。
zh.RISK_2_NAME: AI 层的价值被上游拿走（模型厂商自己就是 agent 平台）
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 它已经在做正确的防守：把 AI 做成成员而不是入口，把权限与审计做成别人绕不过的一层，并用 MCP 让外部 agent 依赖它的上下文。风险在于「依赖是双向的」——它同时依赖上游模型的质量。
zh.RISK_3_NAME: 通知过载与信息密度反噬
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 把「什么该打扰我」做成可训练的一层（而不是再加一层摘要）：以频道/项目为单位设静默、以关注对象为单位设提醒、让 AI 负责「这条要不要现在看」的判断并给出理由。这一层做成了，它就从噪音源变成过滤器。
zh.RISK_4_NAME: AI 额度不透明，长期压低企业续约的确定性
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 把 Slackbot 额度、超额单价、用量面板写清，并给「上限封顶」选项——采购最怕的不是贵，是算不出来。
zh.SHOT_1_CAPTION: Slack 官网首页主视觉：2026 年的主张是 All your people and AI agents working together（取自 slack.com 官方 OG 图）
zh.SHOT_2_CAPTION: Slack AI 功能页主视觉：频道/线程摘要、每日回顾、AI 搜索、文件摘要都在这一层（取自 slack.com/features/ai 官方图）
zh.SHOT_3_CAPTION: Agentforce 进 Slack：Salesforce 的企业 agent 可在频道、DM、线程里被 @ 后执行动作（取自 slack.com/ai-agents 官方图）
zh.SHOT_4_CAPTION: Enterprise Search：一个搜索框搜 Slack + 已连接第三方应用 + 自建数据源，权限感知（取自 slack.com/features/enterprise-search）
zh.SHOT_5_CAPTION: Workflow Builder：触发器 + 步骤 + 条件（官方写 up to 15 conditions）+ 70+ 连接器，Pro 起付费（取自功能页官方图）
zh.SHOT_6_CAPTION: Slack Connect：把外部组织拉进同一批频道与 DM（Pro 以上最多 250 个 orgs），这是它少见的 B 端病毒入口（取自 slack.com/connect）
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Slackbot + Skills：已经在做「理解指令 → 调工具 → 交付产物」的闭环，只是被限制在团队工作流这个边界内。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: 双向 MCP：它同时是 agent 的工具（MCP server）和 agent 的宿主（MCP client）——这是 agent 时代最稀缺的双边位置。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: code channels：[推断] 人 + agent 在频道里共同改代码、看 diff 已经是「agent 进组织」的最小可行形态，下一步才是它自己派活。
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: 两条：一是上游模型厂商把 agent 做成独立产品（用户绕过 Slack 直接跟 agent 说话，Slack 退化为记录层）；二是平台捆绑把「聊天 + AI 摘要」做成免费默认（Teams / Google Chat），让它的 AI 增值难以单独计价。真正剩下的差异只有三样：跨组织网络、应用目录、治理颗粒度。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）把「注意力路由」做成 AI 的第一职责：判断一条消息该不该打扰谁，而不是再写一段摘要。这是它把噪音变成护城河的唯一方向。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把 Skills 变成可市场化交易的资产（作者署名、版本、调用量），它就从「工具」长成「方法论市场」——这也是 Taskade 在做的事（见 014）。
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 可核实：官网定位与主张原文、四档定价金额与功能对照、Slackbot 的 limited trial 与 Enterprise+ 无周上限口径、Flex Credits 与非营利折扣、Workflow Builder 为付费功能与 15 个条件/70+ 连接器、双向 MCP 的两种形态与鉴权方式、Skills 四步发布机制、三个 sitemap 的页数（1,769 / 2,881 / 579）、13 个语种、18 条博客对比页、G2 4.5/40,606 与分布、公开增长史（Wikipedia）。推断并已标注：流量三条腿的权重、单用户频次、北美星与输入/护栏指标、AI 成本结构、竞品的价格与协议细节（本次未核验）。本期没有实测，所有体验类结论均不出。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: [推断] 2,600+ 是「应用数」口径，sitemap 的 2,871 条含历史/下架项；两者都不是活跃安装数。任何按此推算的生态价值都不可信。
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: [推断] 它的收入主力是 Business+ 与 Enterprise+，而不是 Pro：依据是 Slackbot 持续可用与合规套件都从 Business+ 起，且每页并行 Talk to sales。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 它站在三条货架的交口：协作工具（Teams、Google Chat、Discord）、工作 OS / 项目协作（Asana、Trello、Monday、ClickUp——都在它的竞品 vs 页里）、以及 2026 年新出现的一层「agent 托管平台」。位置上它偏协作侧但重心在往 platform 移：比纯聊天多治理与集成，比项目管理工具多对话与实时性，比 agent 平台多一个真实的组织在里面工作。
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 构建过程：Slack 的 AI 不是「一个功能」，是一条从原子到封装的装配线。① 先有 12 个原子：Channel / Canvas / List / Message / Huddle / App / Agent / Slackbot / Workflow / MCP tool / Search / 权限。② 再给一条拼接公式：容器 × 身份 × 权限 × 触发器 × 工具 = 一个工作流——官方在用的四个例子是「Channel + App + OAuth scope + 事件 + Web API」「Channel + Agent + MCP tool + 权限 + @」「Workflow(trigger) + 条件 + 连接器 + 消息步骤」「Huddle + AI 摘要 + Canvas」。③ 最后是三种封装：Template 给人、Slackbot Skills 给团队方法（markdown 或 canvas 写成指令 → 组织级发布）、Agent + 双向 MCP 给机器（Slack MCP Server 让外部 AI 读写 Slack，Slackbot MCP Client 让 Slack 调你的 server）。所以它的统一能力不是某个功能，而是「把任意业务动作变成频道里一次可被 @ 的调用」。
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 三个人的小团队（免费档够用，且 10 个 app 的限制刚好卡住他们）；数据不能出内网的组织（这是 mattermost / stackfield 的活）；只想要「一个便宜好用的聊天工具」的公司（它的定价与治理复杂度是负担）；以及对通知噪音零容忍的团队。
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 护城河是「强」的，但类型要看清：它强在协议与网络（2,600+ 应用按它的身份/权限模型写好、Connect 把外部组织拉进来），不强在 AI（AI 层几乎全是可复制的封装）。真正脆弱的地方只有一处：它的护城河建立在「工作发生在频道里」这个前提上，而 agent 时代的用户可能不再关心「在哪儿说」——那时它的协议层会从资产变成一层昂贵的中间件。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 双向 MCP 的双边位置、2,881 页应用目录、13 语种 1,769 页的大站 SEO、把「个人方法」变成「组织资产」的 Skills 机制、以及从 Pro 到 Enterprise+ 逐级加码的治理颗粒度。
zh.SIX_INTRO: 六维是本系列的主框架：前三条看值不值，后三条看敢不敢用、会不会留下。
zh.AI_TYPE_REASON: 本片判为嵌入。拔电测试：拿走 Slackbot 与 AI 摘要，频道、Connect、Canvas、List、Huddle、Workflow Builder 照常卖。
zh.SIX_1: 替掉的是「这件事该找谁、上次怎么定的」这段往返：原来靠记忆与私聊，现在靠频道历史 + Enterprise Search + @Slackbot。成本从「找人的时间」变成席位费（Free $0 起）——所以它的价值判断从来不是「AI 有多强」，而是「组织够不够大」。
zh.SIX_2: 它啃掉检索、摘要、跨应用取数、把结果写回 Canvas/List；甩回两件：一是权限与接入（app 审批、OAuth scope、管理员批准 MCP），二是治理（信息屏障、法定保留、DLP）。这两件是它最贵的部分，也是它最不愿意替你做的部分——因为那正是它收费的地方。
zh.SIX_3: 能用，但产出需要人确认：Slackbot 在频道里给的是可排序/可筛选/可固定的视图与草稿，不是终稿。本期未实测这一点，只据官方功能页描述，因此不给「能不能直接用」的结论。
zh.SIX_4: 兜底在权限与审批，不在 AI：app approvals、MCP 管理员审批、Enterprise+ 的合规开关构成外层的护栏；但 AI 的产出有没有来源标注与置信度，本次未核验到证据——所以「它凭什么这么说」这一段仍然要靠人。
zh.SIX_5: 大体可逆：消息可编辑/删除、Canvas 有版本、workflow 可停用。不可逆的是那条发到 250 个外部组织（Connect）里的消息——它一旦发出，就同时离开了你的权限边界。对 B 端，这才是真正「错不起」的地方。
zh.SIX_6: 个人换得掉（Discord、Teams、甚至邮件），组织换不掉：历史 + 2,600 应用的集成位 + 治理策略 + 员工的肌肉记忆，四样叠起来，迁移成本远高于订阅费。所以它的留存不是「离不开」，是「换不起」。

en.CATEGORY: B2B Collaboration / AI Work Platform (work OS + agent hosting layer)
en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It doesn't sell chat. It sells turning any business action into one @-able call inside a channel. In 2026 its bet is not a stronger model but becoming the home agents live in — bidirectional MCP, Skills and a permission model, so somebody else's AI can move in.
en.USER_SCALE: Everything verifiable here is a marketing figure: 1B+ messages sent daily, 4M Slack Connect users collaborating with external teams weekly, 3M workflows per day, 1.7M apps actively used weekly (site footnotes credit FY2026 earnings commentary, FY2025 internal data and Salesforce internal data respectively). Marketplace: the site claims 2,600+ apps; the sitemap yields 2,871 app pages (plus 9 collections and 1 index = 2,881). G2: 4.5 / 40,606 reviews, split 5★75% · 4★20% · 3★3% · 2★0% · 1★0%. DAU/MAU, paid seats and ARR are not separately disclosed, so this card does not invent them. The Product Hunt page was blocked by Cloudflare this round — no data used.
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Mature, and mid-way through a second curve. Four public paid tiers (Free / Pro / Business+ / Enterprise+); a 13-language site; 199 customer-story pages; and three separate information architectures — Marketplace (2,881 pages), Help Center (579 pages) and developer docs (3,266 URLs) — each running its own machine. On the AI side it has grown from 'Slack AI summaries' into 'Slackbot + bidirectional MCP + Agentforce + code channels'. Milestones: launched 2013-08 (8,000 customers in 24 hours) → direct listing 2019-06 ($19.5B) → acquired by Salesforce, closed 2021-07-21 (~$27.7B) → ChatGPT integration 2023-03 → Agentforce into Slack 2025-05 → since 2025-06 it blocks long-term LLM indexing/copying of its data.
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Freemium + per-seat subscription + enterprise annual. Free $0 forever (90-day history, up to 10 apps, 1:1 huddles and DMs); Pro $8.75 per user per month (annual $7.25); Business+ $18 (annual $15, Slackbot ongoing); Enterprise+ $45 (annual only, Slackbot with no weekly message limits). AI overage runs through Salesforce Flex Credits; nonprofit and education discounts exist; Frontline is an add-on (all per the pricing FAQ).
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It is a protocol layer that standardises business actions into message-stream atoms. In the AI era it isn't fighting over whose model is best — it's fighting over whose house the agent lives in.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: The unplug test says embedded, not native: remove Slackbot and AI summaries and channels, Slack Connect, Canvas, Lists, Huddles and Workflow Builder all still sell. AI is not the foundation; it is a second floor built on one. The moat isn't the feature list either — it is the access protocol, the permission model and the occupation of the workplace: 2,600+ apps integrate with Slack because Slack defined identity, permissions, events and message format first, and the ecosystem grows features on its behalf. The price: every AI upgrade has to arrive in an existing shape — an agent must be an @-able member, not a new app.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: The moat is the protocol, not the features
en.TLDR_1_BODY: Twelve atoms (Channel / Canvas / List / Message / Huddle / App / Agent / Slackbot / Workflow / MCP tool / Search / permissions) combine into four wrappers: a Template for people, Slackbot Skills for team know-how, Agent + bidirectional MCP for machines, Workflow Builder for processes. It doesn't grow every feature itself — 2,600+ apps do — so its feature list can never catch up, while its access position never moves.
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: The AI pricing unit moved from seats to allowance
en.TLDR_2_BODY: Pricing page, verbatim: Slackbot is a limited trial on Free and Pro, ongoing access continues on Business+ and Enterprise+, only Enterprise+ carries 'no weekly message limits', and overage is bought as Salesforce Flex Credits; Workflow Builder is a paid feature from Pro. Put together, AI here is not an add-on — it is the tier line. That is the most interesting pricing shift in SaaS this year.
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: Traffic is a 13-language mega-site, not one viral post
en.TLDR_3_BODY: Sitemap measurements (2026-11-26): the English marketing site holds 1,769 URLs, replicated across 13 languages (zh-CN 1,478), with /blog/* at 1,179 pages as the single largest block; Marketplace 2,881 pages; Help Center 579 pages (578 articles × 13 languages). Comparison pages come in two layers: product-level /compare/slack-vs-teams and /compare/slack-vs-email, plus a blog cluster /blog/compare/* with 18 entries (13 competitor-vs pages + 4 alternatives pages + 1 German legal page). Classic mega-site + directory + help centre — no single viral hit.
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Product positioning: Slack is the collaboration workplace for teams and enterprises — conversation, documents, tasks, meetings, cross-org collaboration and AI inside one shell. Its 2026 wording is 'The platform agents and AI call home', which defines it as the runtime for agents rather than a chat tool. In plainer terms: for a company of 20 to 20,000 people it solves three recurring questions — where does this get said, who picks it up, and where do we find it later.
en.USER_PROMISE: Homepage H1, verbatim: 'All your people and AI agents working together'; subtitle: 'Slack connects your team. Slackbot multiplies what they can do.' In user language: you no longer decide whether this should be a message, an email or a task — it all lives in one place, and the AI isn't another website either, it's a teammate you can @ in that same place.
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: This is the layer that actually pays. What it buys is 'the channel is the container': one topic, one channel, with people, files, apps and AI inside, and the permission boundary being the channel boundary. Moving up, the reason to pay shifts from unlimited history to governance — multiple workspaces, granular roles, information barriers, legal hold, Discovery API, HIPAA. The site's Solutions menu cuts scenarios into 9 departments × 9 industries × 11 use cases (32 solutions pages), which tells you it sells a workplace per function, not a point tool.
en.SEGMENT_2_NAME: Developers and IT (the people who integrate and govern)
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: This layer doesn't show up on the pricing page, it shows up in the docs: 359 Web API method pages, 121 event pages, 129 scope pages, 46 block elements, 22 blocks, 3,266 doc URLs; 90 CLI command pages, Bolt in three languages, a Deno SDK, 8 official samples. They are its real channel — 2,600+ apps and every internal agent grow out of this layer — and IT is also the person who signs off on Business+ and Enterprise+.
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Slack Connect pulls external organisations into the same channels and DMs (up to 250 orgs on Pro and above), described on the site as moving conversations out of siloed email threads. The strategic value isn't revenue, it's distribution: every cross-company collaboration is a product impression, and the other company often doesn't use Slack yet. This is the rare case of a viral loop built for B2B.
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Keep one thing said, decided and tracked in one place instead of hauling it between email, IM, docs and tickets.
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Don't miss the important message, and don't drown in messages. The thing 5-star G2 reviewers complain about is nearly always the same: too many notifications, important updates buried in busy channels, old context hard to find. It sells the feeling 'I can find it'; the lived experience is often 'I have to dig for it'.
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: Be the person in the org who knows where to ask and who owns what; externally, be the partner who gets invited into the channel.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: The team goes from 8 to 20 people and WeChat, email or hallway talk starts dropping context: the same question asked three times, new hires needing a human guide. Slack's trigger isn't 'I want a chat tool', it's 'we need a place where this accumulates'.
en.FREQUENCY: Always on during the workday — dozens to hundreds of touches a day; the site claims 1B+ messages sent daily (FY2026 earnings commentary). Per-user frequency is not disclosed.
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Desktop, mobile and web; meetings happen inside a channel as a Huddle; action items land in Canvas or Lists; cross-company work runs through Connect; retrieval runs through Enterprise Search and AI search; execution runs through Workflow Builder, Slackbot and @-mentioned agents; data exits through the MCP server, Web API and Events.
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: The trigger isn't 'I want AI', it's 'someone has to pick this up'. Slack's cleverness is that it built no new entry point for AI: every AI capability lives in an existing container — the composer, the channel, the canvas, the list. The user learns nothing new, they just type @Slackbot instead of @a-colleague.
en.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: Type @ in the composer, or let it run itself
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: One composer carries three actions: @ an agent / run a workflow / turn the message into a List row. Workflow Builder supports triggers, steps and conditions (the site says 'up to 15 conditions') across 70+ connectors; Slackbot can call your own MCP server with four auth modes (none / Slack identity / DCR / manual OAuth). Collapsing the action entry points is what turns AI into a habit rather than a feature.
en.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: Answer, record and next step all stay in the conversation
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: You don't switch to another screen to see the result: Slackbot's output can be a sortable, filterable, pinnable view inside the channel, a Huddle produces notes and action items when it ends, and a Canvas can hold a workflow. Keeping output where the work happens is the biggest difference between Slack and every AI product that asks you to open a new app.
en.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: The channel thickens and history becomes an asset
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: You come back not to chat again but to ask which channel decided that last time. Channels, threads, Canvas and Lists form organisational memory that cannot be moved, and Enterprise Search stitches it to connected third-party apps. That the free plan caps history at 90 days is the clearest proof that history is what this business sells.
en.LOOP_FREQ: Dozens to hundreds of times a day ([inferred] from 1B+ messages daily divided across enterprise working days; per-user frequency and DAU are not disclosed).
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The same trigger repeats: something happens and someone has to catch it in a channel. The product converts that from 'DM a person' into 'say it once in the open', which turns one-to-many into many-to-many. That is its real product thesis — and the reason it generates notification overload.
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What it teaches is that work doesn't need to be archived somewhere else: the conversation is the record and @ is the execution. Use it long enough and people start judging whether something deserves doing by whether it has a channel.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Traffic and exposure: three legs running in parallel, weighted roughly as follows ([inferred] from page structure and CTA design). (1) In-product PLG and team self-propagation: every page's CTA is 'Get started' with no sales gate, templates drop into a workspace in one click, and Skills publish at org level. (2) Mega-site SEO: 1,769 English marketing URLs + 2,881 Marketplace pages + 579 help pages, replicated across 13 languages, with 1,179 blog posts as the largest single block. (3) The Salesforce channel: co-branded as a Salesforce company, Slackbot inside Lightning, Flex Credits sold through Salesforce, and a parallel 'Talk to sales' on every page. Organic share of traffic, CAC by channel and the share of signups from Marketplace are all unverified — no guesses offered.
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: The most aha-shaped moment in the official narrative: you @Slackbot in a channel, it calls your own MCP server, and the tool result comes back in the thread — not another app opened, just one more teammate. Not tested this round; this point rests on the official feature page and docs, and is not a hands-on conclusion.
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Yes, structurally — it just doesn't look like virality. Slack Connect pulls external organisations into the same channels (250 orgs on Pro+), so cross-company collaboration is itself exposure; org-level publishing of templates and Slackbot Skills turns one person's method into something the whole team runs, which is internal propagation. Sharing data is not disclosed; this is [inferred].
en.RETENTION_1: Channels, threads, Canvas and Lists form organisational memory; leaving means leaving the memory behind (the free plan caps it at 90 days, which is exactly what paid tiers sell back).
en.RETENTION_2: Once 2,600+ integrations and their OAuth grants are wired in, switching means redoing every connection and every approval.
en.RETENTION_3: The governance layer — information barriers, legal hold, Discovery API, DLP, app approvals — is why IT renews, and the hardest part to move.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Free $0 forever (90-day history, 10 apps) → the team outgrows it and needs unlimited history and apps (Pro $8.75) → it needs ongoing Slackbot plus compliance (Business+ $18) → it needs multi-SAML, data residency and no weekly Slackbot cap (Enterprise+ $45). Every step is bound to something only an organisation needs, which is the standard path from individual use to enterprise payment.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: A third-party app lists in Marketplace for distribution → each app page contributes long-tail search (2,871 app pages in the sitemap) → a user installs Slack because of that app → the app's author becomes a Slack reseller. Slack writes no extra content; the directory grows for it. The fragility: the moment it tightens review or API access (it began blocking long-term LLM indexing in 2025-06), the loop slows down.
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: The product's container and its permission boundary: one topic per channel, with people, files, apps and AI inside. The site calls them flexible, transparent spaces for working together. Every AI capability is built on this container rather than beside it.
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: Pulls external organisations into the same channels and DMs (up to 250 orgs on Pro+), positioned as moving conversations out of siloed email threads. A rare B2B viral entry: the partner is made a user.
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Canvas is the document surface inside a channel and the instruction carrier for Slackbot Skills (the docs say 'with a canvas you own'); List is the task table in the conversation, readable and writable by workflows and CRUD-able through the MCP server. These two are the bridge from chat to work.
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: Instant audio/video inside a channel plus asynchronous recording. When a Huddle ends, AI produces notes, action items and who said what. A meeting stops being separate software and becomes a raised hand in the channel.
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: Slackbot is the team-level AI teammate (acting across apps: research, building workflows, building dashboards, reports and polls, updating records, drafting content); an Agent is a member-level entity you can @. Both grow capabilities through Skills (markdown or canvas instructions published at org level) and bidirectional MCP. This is where its 2026 product gravity sits.
en.SURFACE_6_NAME: Workflow Builder + Enterprise Search (orchestration and retrieval)
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: Orchestration: triggers, steps and conditions (up to 15) across 70+ connectors, with AI response, agent-conversation and custom-code steps, paid from Pro. Retrieval: one search box across Slack, connected apps and custom sources (Custom Sources API), permission-aware. The first turns repeated processes into automation, the second turns memory into a query — those two are what 'work OS' actually means.
en.ENTITY_1: Workspace / Org (the unit of billing and permission)
en.ENTITY_3: Message / Thread (the smallest unit of conversation and its replies)
en.ENTITY_4: Canvas / List / Workflow (document, structured records, automation)
en.ENTITY_5: App / Agent / Skill / MCP server (identities and tools that can be @-ed)
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: The spine is the channel: everything enters through a channel, then strings sideways into search, Connect and governance. The upside is zero learning cost — a channel is already the team's mental unit. The cost is that the product has no canvas of its own; all value is stored in whether the conversation happens here. That is exactly why AI had to become a member of the channel: a new surface would break the spine, a new member doesn't.
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Structurally it is a three-part layout: channel list on the left, search on top, composer at the bottom — and the composer doubles as the entry for messages, workflows, agent calls and file uploads. Collapsing every action into one box is its most economical and most effective interaction decision. Not tested this round; this paragraph rests on official feature pages and docs, with no hands-on claims.
en.CRAFT_1_NAME: Make AI a member, not a button
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: Slackbot's identity is a teammate you can @, not an icon in a toolbar. That single choice buys three things: the AI has permissions, context and history; the human never switches surface; and its output in a channel is visible to others, which makes it reusable.
en.CRAFT_2_NAME: Three wrappers, three kinds of buyer
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Templates sell to teams that don't want to configure from zero (pre-configured channel + canvas + list + workflow); Slackbot Skills sell to people who already have a method (one markdown file or one canvas → org-level publish → one click for the whole team); Agent + bidirectional MCP sells to organisations with engineers. The same atoms, three packages, three buyers.
en.CRAFT_3_NAME: The mechanism that turns personal craft into organisational assets
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: Skills runs four steps: write instructions in markdown or a canvas → create → update → publish at org level (API name admin.slackbot.skills.publish) → land in the member library. This is the standard shape of productised knowledge: rules written as files, published as capability, called on demand. It converts a senior colleague's judgement from folklore into an executable asset.
en.CRAFT_4_NAME: Bidirectional MCP: both server and client
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: One side is the Slack MCP Server (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp, remote HTTP + OAuth) letting external AIs like Claude and Cursor read and write messages, channels, Canvas and Lists. The other side is the Slackbot MCP Client, letting Slack connect to your own remote MCP server and auto-discover and call its tools. Your AI may enter my house; my AI may visit yours. That is the hardest step for any platform product to copy in 2026.
en.CRAFT_5_NAME: Turn AI usage into the pricing tier line
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Slackbot is a limited trial on Free and Pro, ongoing on Business+ and Enterprise+, 'no weekly message limits' only on Enterprise+, with overage through Salesforce Flex Credits. The exact numbers are not published — an undefined allowance is itself pricing power. The lesson for everyone else: pricing on AI execution rather than headcount alone will be the SaaS default in 2026.
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Every craft decision points at one sentence: let new capability arrive in an existing shape. An agent is a member, a skill is a file, an automation is a step in a channel. The user learns nothing new — they just repeat an old action.
en.TTV_LABEL: Time to value: not measured this round (no hands-on test was run; receiving the first message is not counted as value, and no minutes are claimed)
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: Only the structure is verifiable: sign up → create a workspace → invite members → create a channel → install an app or configure a workflow. The real aha usually comes from a colleague, not the product (someone replies in the channel you created). Onboarding data is not disclosed, so no time figure is given.
en.COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: medium (not measured; the verifiable structure is four containers coexisting in one interface — channels, threads, canvas, lists)
en.DELIGHT_1: Templates drop a whole workspace skeleton in one click — channel + canvas + list + workflow — instead of a blank page (35 templates across 14 categories).
en.DELIGHT_2: A Huddle ends and the notes and action items already exist; a meeting needs no second application.
en.DELIGHT_3: @ an agent and a code channel opens, with people, teammates and the agent looking at the diff together.
en.DELIGHT_LABEL: Delight: one-click workspaces, meetings that leave a record, agents that are channel members
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: public sentiment is steady (G2 4.5 / 40,606 with 1★ and 2★ at 0% each) and the enterprise trust layer is tiered (information barriers, legal hold, Discovery API, HIPAA from Business+; multi-SAML and data residency on Enterprise+). But the real trust bottleneck isn't security, it's noise: the loudest complaint among 5-star users is that important things get buried.
en.STRUGGLE_1: Notification overload and buried information. G2, verbatim: 'The notification overload can get pretty overwhelming once you're in a few active channel, important updates get buried fast' — and 5-star reviewers repeat the same line. This is the direct cost of 'everything goes into a channel'.
en.STRUGGLE_2: The free-tier wall is hard: 90-day message history, at most 10 apps, 1:1 huddles. G2 names it: 'the 90-day message history limit on the free tier is really annoying'.
en.STRUGGLE_3: Learning curve and interface complexity. G2, verbatim: 'The interface was too hard to use. Not user-friendly enough'; another review says it is incredibly hard to follow unless you are on it 24x7.
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Friction: notification overload, the free-tier wall, the learning curve
en.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Freemium + per-seat subscription + enterprise annual (AI allowance as the tier line)
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Free $0 (90-day history / 10 apps / 1:1 huddles and external DMs / Basic AI); Pro $8.75 per user per month, $7.25 annual (unlimited history, unlimited apps, group huddles, up to 250 external orgs); Business+ $18, $15 annual (ongoing Slackbot + admin and compliance suite); Enterprise+ $45, annual only, contact sales (no weekly Slackbot limit, Enterprise search, multi-SAML, data residency). Promo prices (Pro $4.38, Business+ $9 for three months) and Flex Credits overage are both spelled out in the pricing FAQ.
en.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: The entry is free enough to spread itself; the money is in governance and AI allowance
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: The free plan is the minimum a real team can work in (90-day history + 10 apps + 1:1 meetings), landing exactly where a small team is fine and a growing team is not. Three paid steps: unlimited history and apps (Pro) → ongoing Slackbot plus compliance (Business+) → multi-SAML, data residency, no weekly cap (Enterprise+). It doesn't sell features; it sells the things an organisation must have once it grows.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free: 90-day message history, up to 10 apps, 1:1 huddles, 1:1 external DMs, Basic AI (summaries / Slackbot trial / AI workflow generation / AI search / daily recaps / file summaries). Paid: Pro buys unlimited history, unlimited apps, group huddles and up to 250 external orgs; Business+ buys ongoing Slackbot plus governance (multiple workspaces, granular roles, information barriers, legal hold, Discovery API, HIPAA); Enterprise+ buys no weekly Slackbot limit, Enterprise search, multi-SAML and data residency. Workflow Builder is paid from Pro, and AI overage runs through Flex Credits.
en.UX_MON_HEADLINE: Are experience and monetisation aligned, or fighting?
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Broadly aligned, with one new crack in 2026. Aligned: the free plan sits exactly where a team naturally hits a wall (history, app count, group meetings), and every paywall lands on something only a bigger organisation needs (governance, compliance, AI allowance). Fighting: AI pricing moved from seats to a Slackbot allowance, and the allowance numbers aren't published — buyers cannot budget their AI spend, and procurement converts that uncertainty into a discount at renewal. A second tension: whether Workflow Builder counts as free-tier capability is contradictory in its own pages — the feature page calls it paid, the free tier lists AI workflow generation.
en.COMP_1_D1: The same enterprise employees: companies already on Microsoft 365
en.COMP_1_D2: Built into the Microsoft 365 stack (same account as Outlook / SharePoint / Office), meetings via Teams; its external protocol details were not verified this round
en.COMP_1_D3: Enterprise volume licensing and IT procurement — it arrives by default with M365
en.COMP_1_D4: Not verified this round (Slack lists it at /compare/slack-vs-teams and first in its 13 blog competitor-vs pages)
en.COMP_2_D1: Workspace customers: teams already using Gmail / Drive / Meet
en.COMP_2_D2: Same stack as Gmail, Drive and Meet; the account system is the permission system
en.COMP_2_D3: The Workspace default — zero distribution cost
en.COMP_3_D1: Communities and hobby groups first, now seeping into small-team work
en.COMP_3_D2: Channels plus voice rooms, designed for presence, not permissions and governance
en.COMP_3_D3: Community word of mouth and creator ecosystems; almost no enterprise sales
en.COMP_4_NAME: Self-hosted and compliance substitutes (Mattermost / Chatwork / Line Works / Stackfield)
en.COMP_4_D1: Organisations whose data cannot leave the intranet, or whose local market is held by a local product
en.COMP_4_D2: Self-hosted or locally deployed; trading features for data staying home
en.COMP_4_D3: Public-sector procurement, regional channels, open-source communities
en.COMP_4_D4: Not verified this round (all four appear in Slack's own blog competitor list, so Slack counts them as rivals)
en.COMP_OWN_D1: Team collaboration workplace + agent hosting layer
en.COMP_OWN_D2: Bidirectional MCP (server + client) + 2,600 apps + @-able agents + Real-Time Search API
en.COMP_OWN_D3: 13-language mega-site (1,769 English URLs) + 2,881 Marketplace pages + 579 help pages + the Salesforce channel
en.COMP_OWN_D4: Four public tiers, Slackbot allowance as the tier line, Flex Credits for overage — but the actual allowance numbers are not published
en.COMP_INTRO: The list isn't guesswork; it comes from Slack's own moves. Product-level comparison pages are only two (/compare/slack-vs-teams, /compare/slack-vs-email), but the blog cluster /blog/compare/* holds 18, of which 13 are competitor-vs pages — asana, chatwork, clickup, discord, google-chat, line-works, mattermost, microsoft-teams, monday, stackfield, trello, whatsapp, zoom — plus 4 alternatives pages (teams / discord / google-chat / trello). In other words: Microsoft Teams is the frontal battlefield, Google Chat and Discord are the flanks, and mattermost / chatwork / line-works / stackfield are the defence against localisation and self-hosting. Competitor prices were not verified this round and are not invented here.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Three things rivals can't close quickly: bidirectional MCP (most competitors integrate one way; Slack shipped both server and client); the thickness of the app directory (2,600 apps, 2,871 sitemap pages, each app carrying its own long-tail page); and governance granularity (information barriers, legal hold, Discovery API, app approvals) — the real staircase from Pro to Enterprise+.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Three gaps: bundling (Teams arrives with M365, Google Chat with Workspace; nobody buys the same thing twice); notification overload (its own 5-star users complain, and that is a structural problem it grew itself, while products like Discord treat noise as atmosphere); and opaque AI allowance (Slackbot limits unpublished mean procurement can't do the maths, which hands rivals a 'bundled price is easier to budget' pitch).
en.CHANNEL_1: Two SEO tracks: localisation and high intent. 13 language sites (1,769 English URLs, 1,478 zh-CN), with 1,179 blog posts as the largest single block; two product-level comparison pages plus 13 blog competitor-vs pages and 4 alternatives pages; and pricing itself split into four landers — /pricing/free, /pricing/pro, /pricing/businessplus, /pricing/paid-vs-free — to catch plan-level searches.
en.CHANNEL_2: PLG free tier and team self-propagation: every page CTA is 'Get started' with no sales gate, templates drop into a workspace in one click, and Skills publish at org level — 'one person's method becomes a one-click team capability' is propagation by design.
en.CHANNEL_3: The Salesforce enterprise channel plus a partner programme: co-branded as a Salesforce company, Slackbot inside Lightning, Flex Credits sold through Salesforce, alongside Partner Program, Partner Offers, Slack Certified and 199 customer stories for procurement-stage buyers.
en.FRICTION_1_TITLE: Notification overload: the price of 'everything in a channel'
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: The complaints from 5-star G2 reviewers are strikingly consistent: important updates buried, old context hard to find, notifications distracting. This is not a bug; it is the other side of the design choice that makes the product transparent. For its AI this is the real question: summaries and daily recaps just add a layer on top of the noise. The real fix is deciding what deserves to interrupt whom.
en.FRICTION_2_TITLE: The free-tier wall sits exactly where a team starts growing
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: 90-day history + 10 apps + 1:1 huddles: each item looks reasonable, together they mean 'delightful for a tiny team, blocked for a real one'. G2 names the history limit as annoying. That is intent, not defect — but it also means it earns almost nothing from three-person teams, so revenue depends on the customer's hiring pace.
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: G2, verbatim: 'The interface was too hard to use. Not user-friendly enough'; another review says unless you are on it 24x7 it is incredibly hard to follow. For an internal communication tool that is another way of saying the information architecture has outgrown the organisation's information volume.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Opaque AI pricing: the allowance is not published
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: The pricing page only says Slackbot is a limited trial on Free and Pro and has no weekly message limits on Enterprise+; the numbers aren't given, and overage goes through Salesforce Flex Credits. For procurement, that makes AI unbudgetable; for competitors, it is the best opening line available. One contradiction is also unresolved: Workflow Builder is called a paid feature on its feature page while the free tier lists AI workflow generation.
en.METRICS_INTRO: No operating metrics are separately disclosed. What follows separates verifiable public facts (prices, sitemap page counts, G2 rating distribution, official marketing figures) from [inferred] 'what it should be watching' — the latter is not real data.
en.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: Weekly completed actions inside channels (agent invocations + workflows run to completion + List items closed) ([inferred])
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [inferred] It charges per seat and prices on 'does the work happen here': message volume proves busyness, actions prove it is a workplace. The north star shouldn't be DAU — Slack's DAU saturated long ago; what 2026 has to prove is whether the AI actually gets used.
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: Free → paid history unlock (how often messages older than 90 days are read)
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: The only free-tier wall that actually hurts is 90-day history. A team that searched past 90 days has a genuine memory requirement; that behaviour predicts payment better than signups do.
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: Slackbot weekly actives and the number of org-level Skills published
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Slackbot is its only AI revenue tier line; Skills published at org level show whether personal method became an organisational asset — its most distinctive retention mechanism against every other AI assistant.
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: Marketplace install depth (still in use 30 days after install)
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: The 2,881-page app directory is its long tail and its moat, but the directory is only worth as much as its apps are used, not as many as exist. Install-without-use turns an ecosystem from an asset into noise.
en.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: Notifications per user per day + delay until a critical message is read
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Every 5-star G2 reviewer complains about the same thing: important things get buried. Notification volume is growth's most honest counter-metric — more notifications can raise activity while lowering value. Without this guardrail, AI summaries just make the noise more expensive.
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: No public paid-seat churn, ARR breakdown or per-message inference cost [inferred]
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [inferred] The claim that Slackbot is a fixed per-seat cost rather than token-billed means Slack is absorbing inference cost uncertainty on the customer's behalf; the free tier uses AI too, so free users keep burning money. Watching only activity and reviews hides that the more AI gets used, the thinner the margin. A second blind spot: since 2025-06 it blocks long-term LLM indexing, which protects its data but erodes its visibility inside AI answers — and that will never show up in a product metric.
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Protocol and permissions 9, distribution and directory 9, occupation of the workplace 9, AI capability 6, independent pricing power 5 (a Salesforce company), anti-scraping 7 — weighted 8. Features can be copied; '2,600 apps already written against your identity and permission model' cannot.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: From conversation to execution: Workflow Builder, Slackbot's live artifacts and Slack CRM wire the end of a conversation into process and business objects.
en.HORIZONTAL_2: From people to agents: Agent, code channels and bidirectional MCP extend the idea of 'colleague' beyond humans ([inferred] the only direction that escapes 'yet another chat tool').
en.VERTICAL_1: 9 departments × 9 industries: Frontline, Engineering, IT, customer service, sales, project management, marketing, HR, security, plus manufacturing, financial services, retail, public sector, education and healthcare.
en.VERTICAL_2: 11 use-case pages (project management, client collaboration, effective meetings, sales pipeline, internal comms, project tracking, lead management, team productivity, onboarding, time tracking, finding answers faster) — it has laid a page for every role that collaborates.
en.PLATFORM_1: The open interfaces are already there: Slack MCP Server (remote HTTP + OAuth), Slackbot MCP Client (4 auth modes), Web API (359 method pages), Events (121 pages), Real-Time Search API, Block Kit, Bolt in three languages, a Deno SDK, a CLI and 8 official samples.
en.PLATFORM_2: [inferred] Its platform play is to be the hosting layer for agents: not fighting over who is the assistant, but over where the assistant lives. Being part of Salesforce makes this easier, not harder — Salesforce needs an enterprise venue where agents can actually land, and Slack is that venue.
en.OPP_1_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Copy 'Skills → organisational asset' as a knowledge product
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How: instructions in markdown or a canvas → publish at org level → one click for the whole team. Copy Slackbot Skills' four steps (create / update / publish / add to member library) but land them in a narrow scenario, such as one role's fixed process. Why: it is the shortest path from 'a senior colleague's judgement' to an executable asset, and most knowledge products stop at 'the document is stored' without ever reaching 'the capability gets called'.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Build the protocol or plugin first, not another interface
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: How: ship the product as an MCP server plus a Skill pack so it gets called inside someone else's surface (Claude, Cursor, Slackbot can all be hosts) instead of demanding one more install. Why: Slack proved that defining identity, permissions, events and message format makes the ecosystem grow features for you — for a small team, it is the only way to borrow someone else's distribution.
en.OPP_3_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Price on execution, but publish the allowance
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: How: add a tier priced by AI execution rather than headcount — and publish the allowance numbers, the overage unit price and a usage dashboard. Why: Slack has already moved the tier line from seats to Slackbot allowance but keeps the numbers private, which is both its pricing power and its procurement friction. Copy the direction, invert the transparency — the cheapest differentiation available.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: Its bet: don't build the strongest AI, build the house AI has to live in
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: Three moves stacked: make AI a channel member (Slackbot / Agent / Skills) rather than a new surface; use bidirectional MCP so external agents can come in and go out; and use permissions and governance to make 'let an agent touch real data' an enterprise-safe decision. The first two are product moves; the third is the actual bet — because what stops an agent is never capability, it is authorisation. The price: it must keep compromising, since keeping 2,600 apps compatible means every AI capability has to fit an old shape, and the ecosystem holds its innovation speed hostage.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Endgame: work has no entry point, only 'who gets called'
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: If agents really become colleagues, 'open a work app' disappears: a person speaks, the agent calls tools, leaves records and finds the next executor. In that world the winner is not the one with the best model but the one holding identity, permissions, context and audit — all four. Slack is closest to that endgame but is missing two pieces: its own model (it chose to partner instead) and context outside Slack (blocking LLM indexing in 2025-06 shows it won't hand context over). Those two decide whether it is the agent's home or the agent's dormitory.
en.RISK_INTRO: Risks ordered by likelihood × impact; severity is my judgement, not a company disclosure.
en.RISK_1_NAME: Bundling: Teams and Google Chat make chat a free default
en.RISK_1_MIT: Hold the three things bundling can't do: cross-company collaboration (the Connect network), the thickness of the app directory, and the openness of bidirectional MCP. And sell governance as the headline — information barriers and legal hold are the hardest layer for a bundled product to build.
en.RISK_2_NAME: AI value captured upstream (model vendors are becoming agent platforms)
en.RISK_2_MIT: It is already defending correctly: AI as member rather than entry point, permissions and audit as a layer nobody can route around, and MCP making external agents depend on its context. The risk is that dependence runs both ways — it also depends on upstream model quality.
en.RISK_3_NAME: Notification overload and information density backfiring
en.RISK_3_MIT: Make 'what deserves to interrupt me' a trainable layer instead of another summary: quiet hours per channel or project, alerts per followed object, and an AI that decides whether this needs attention now and explains why. Done well, it turns the noise source into the filter.
en.RISK_4_NAME: Opaque AI allowance erodes enterprise renewal certainty
en.RISK_4_MIT: Publish the Slackbot allowance, the overage unit price and a usage dashboard, and offer a hard cap. Procurement doesn't fear cost; it fears arithmetic it cannot do.

en.SHOT_2_CAPTION: Slack AI feature page hero: channel and thread summaries, daily recaps, AI search and file summaries live here (official image from slack.com/features/ai)
en.SHOT_3_CAPTION: Agentforce in Slack: Salesforce's enterprise agent can be @-mentioned in channels, DMs and threads to execute actions (official image from slack.com/ai-agents)
en.SHOT_4_CAPTION: Enterprise Search: one box across Slack, connected third-party apps and custom sources, permission-aware (official image from slack.com/features/enterprise-search)
en.SHOT_5_CAPTION: Workflow Builder: triggers, steps and conditions ('up to 15 conditions') across 70+ connectors, paid from Pro (official feature-page image)

en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Slackbot + Skills: already runs the loop of understanding an instruction, calling tools and delivering an artifact — just bounded to team workflows.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: Bidirectional MCP: simultaneously the agent's tool (MCP server) and the agent's host (MCP client) — the scarcest two-sided position in the agent era.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: code channels: [inferred] people, teammates and agents editing code together and reviewing diffs in a channel is the minimum viable shape of 'an agent joins the org'; assigning work itself comes later.
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: Two: upstream model vendors ship agents as standalone products (users talk to the agent directly and Slack degrades into a record layer); and platform bundling makes chat plus AI summaries a free default (Teams, Google Chat), which makes its AI premium hard to charge for. What remains as differentiation is exactly three things: the cross-org network, the app directory and governance granularity.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (My judgement) Make attention routing the AI's first job — deciding which message should interrupt whom, instead of writing another summary. That is the only route from noise source to moat.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (My judgement) Turn Skills into tradable assets (author, version, invocation count) and it grows from tool to marketplace of methods — which is exactly what Taskade is doing (see 014).
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Verifiable: the site's positioning copy, the four tier prices and feature mapping, the Slackbot limited-trial and Enterprise+ no-weekly-limit wording, Flex Credits and nonprofit discounts, Workflow Builder as paid with 15 conditions and 70+ connectors, the two shapes of bidirectional MCP and their auth modes, the four-step Skills publishing mechanism, the three sitemap counts (1,769 / 2,881 / 579), the 13 languages, the 18 blog comparison pages, G2 4.5/40,606 with distribution, and the public growth history (Wikipedia). Inferred and flagged: the weighting of the three traffic legs, per-user frequency, north-star and input/guardrail metrics, AI cost structure, and competitor prices and protocol details (not verified this round). No hands-on test was run, so no experience conclusions are given.
en.ASSUMPTION_1: [inferred] '2,600+' counts apps, and the 2,871 sitemap entries include historical and delisted ones; neither equals active installations. Any ecosystem value derived from them is unreliable.
en.ASSUMPTION_2: [inferred] The revenue core is Business+ and Enterprise+, not Pro: ongoing Slackbot and the compliance suite both start at Business+, and every page carries a parallel 'Talk to sales'.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: It stands where three shelves intersect: collaboration tools (Teams, Google Chat, Discord), work OS / project collaboration (Asana, Trello, Monday, ClickUp — all in its competitor-vs pages), and the 2026 layer of 'agent hosting platform'. It leans collaboration-side but its centre of gravity is moving toward platform: more governance and integration than plain chat, more conversation and real-time than project tools, and one thing no agent platform has — a real organisation already working inside it.
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: How the AI is built: Slack's AI is not a feature, it is an assembly line from atoms to wrappers. (1) Twelve atoms first: Channel / Canvas / List / Message / Huddle / App / Agent / Slackbot / Workflow / MCP tool / Search / permissions. (2) Then one composition formula — container × identity × permissions × trigger × tool = a workflow — with four examples the company itself uses: 'Channel + App + OAuth scope + events + Web API', 'Channel + Agent + MCP tool + permissions + @', 'Workflow(trigger) + conditions + connector + message step', 'Huddle + AI summary + Canvas'. (3) Finally three wrappers: Template for people, Slackbot Skills for team method (write instructions in markdown or a canvas, then publish at org level), and Agent + bidirectional MCP for machines (Slack MCP Server lets external AI read and write Slack; Slackbot MCP Client lets Slack call your server). So the unified capability isn't any single feature — it is turning any business action into one @-able call in a channel.
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Three-person teams (the free plan is enough and the 10-app cap blocks them anyway); organisations whose data cannot leave the intranet (that is mattermost / stackfield territory); companies that just want a cheap, good chat tool (its pricing and governance complexity is overhead); and teams with zero tolerance for notification noise.
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: The moat is strong, but the type matters: strong on protocol and network (2,600+ apps written against its identity and permission model, Connect pulling external orgs in), not strong on AI (the AI layer is almost entirely copyable packaging). Only one soft spot: the moat assumes work happens in channels. In an agent era people may stop caring where they said it — at which point the protocol layer turns from asset into expensive middleware.
en.FINAL_WINS: Its two-sided MCP position, a 2,881-page app directory, a 13-language 1,769-page SEO footprint, the Skills mechanism that turns personal method into organisational assets, and governance granularity that ratchets up from Pro to Enterprise+.
en.SIX_INTRO: Six dimensions are the main framework: the first three are about value, the last three about trust and switching cost.
en.AI_TYPE_REASON: Classified as embedded. Unplug test: remove Slackbot and AI summaries and channels, Connect, Canvas, Lists, Huddles and Workflow Builder still sell.
en.SIX_1: What it replaces is the round trip of 'who owns this and how did we decide last time': memory and DMs become channel history plus Enterprise Search plus @Slackbot. Cost moves from searching for a person to a seat fee (from $0), which is why the value judgement is never 'how good is the AI' but 'is the organisation big enough'.
en.SIX_2: It eats retrieval, summarisation, cross-app data fetching and writing results back into Canvas and Lists. It hands back two things: permissions and access (app approvals, OAuth scopes, admin approval for MCP), and governance (information barriers, legal hold, DLP). Those two are its most expensive parts and the parts it least wants to do for you — because that is what it charges for.
en.SIX_3: Usable, but output needs human confirmation: what Slackbot produces in a channel is a sortable, filterable, pinnable view and a draft, not a final document. Not tested this round, so no verdict on 'can you ship it as-is' is offered.
en.SIX_4: The safety net is permissions and approval, not the AI: app approvals, admin approval for MCP and Enterprise+ compliance switches form the outer rail. Whether AI output carries source attribution or confidence was not verified this round — so the 'why does it say this' question still falls to a human.
en.SIX_5: Mostly reversible: messages can be edited or deleted, Canvas has versions, workflows can be disabled. What is irreversible is the message sent into a Connect channel shared with 250 external orgs — once sent, it has left your permission boundary. For B2B, that is where 'you can't afford to be wrong' actually lives.
en.SIX_6: An individual can switch (Discord, Teams, even email); an organisation cannot: history + 2,600 integration slots + governance policies + muscle memory add up to a migration cost far above the subscription. So retention isn't 'can't leave' — it's 'can't afford to leave'.

extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
这份名单不是猜的，全部取自它自己的动作：官网产品级对比页只放了两个（/compare/slack-vs-teams、/compare/slack-vs-email），但博客级 /blog/compare/* 有 18 条——13 个竞品 vs 页（asana、chatwork、clickup、discord、google-chat、line-works、mattermost、microsoft-teams、monday、stackfield、trello、whatsapp、zoom）+ 4 个 alternatives 页（teams / discord / google-chat / trello）+ 1 个德语法务页。换句话说：它把谁当对手，写在博客目录里。

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
Microsoft Teams同一批企业员工：已经在用 Microsoft 365 的公司同一个入口：聊天 + 会议 + 文件，长在 M365 同一个账号体系里它唯一的「产品级」对比对象（/compare/slack-vs-teams）。威胁不是功能，是「已经付过钱了」

Asana / Trello / Monday / ClickUp要「项目被跟踪」而不是「对话被看见」的团队任务与流程这一段链路（Slack 用 List + Workflow 去接）四家各有 vs 页。它的应对不是做更强的项目管理，而是把项目搬进频道（List + 模板）
